name: Tod Man Khao Pod (Thai Corn Fritters)

instructions.primary_message: Remove corn kernels from cobs (you should have about 2 1/2 cups kernels). Pour oil to a depth of 2.5 cm in a wok, small Dutch oven, or large heavy-bottomed saucepan. Heat oil over medium heat to 149°C (300°F). Line a large platter or rimmed baking sheet with paper towels; set aside.

Reserve half of corn kernels and place other half in a blender or food processor along with red curry paste, egg, rice flour, baking powder, and salt; blend until just smooth and batter is loose, about 30 seconds. Transfer mixture to a medium bowl.

Stack makrut lime leaves (or basil leaves) and roll them up tightly. Slice the roll crosswise as finely as possible. Fold makrut lime leaf strips into corn batter along with reserved whole corn kernels.

Working in batches of about 6 at a time, drop 1 tablespoon size portions of corn batter very gently into oil. It helps to drop the batter closer to the oil’s surface to keep the fritter batter together. Do not over-fill pot. Once the fritters float to the top, continue to fry, flipping occasionally, until fritters are golden brown all over and start to darken around the edges, 3 to 4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer them to the paper towel-lined platter. Return oil temperature to 150°C and repeat with remaining batches of fritters.
Allow last batch of fritters to cool slightly before serving them with Thai sweet chili sauce.

schema_metadata.keywords: basil, corn, curry, egg, fritter, kaffir lime, quick

description: With crispy edges and a chewy interior, these sweet and slightly spicy fresh corn fritters are the perfect easy party appetizer.
notes:
Optional substitutions: makrut lime leaves → ¼ cup Thai basil leaves

Notes: Frozen corn kernels can also be used in this recipe. Make sure to thaw them completely and squeeze as much moisture out of them as possible.
author: Leela Punyaratabandhu
